messages:
ashley_support: FYI customer Acme reports repeated tail-latency spikes and intermittent 503s on /v1/embeddings since yesterday evening. They say it started after rolling a client change that batches small and large requests together.

liam_runtime: Can you paste a short repro or logs? any error traces from the batcher or runtime?

ashley_support: Paste from customer: 
```
client: acme-api-v2
requests/sec: ~120
payloads: mix of 32-token texts and occasional 20k-char documents
errors: 503 (embed timeout) + 409 dim-mismatch for some retries
observed tail p99: 2.3s -> spikes to 8-12s periodically
billing: tokens billed spike x3 since retries started
```

ashley_support: They included a minimal repro that blasts embeddings with concurrency=64, interleaving short/long inputs. Attached here as inline repro.

ashley_support: Repro (python):
```
# gist simplified
import requests, time, random
url = 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings'
auth = {'Authorization': 'Bearer REDACTED'}
def make(i):
    if i % 10 == 0:
        text = 'A'*20000
    else:
        text = 'short text %d' % i
    return requests.post(url, json={'input': text, 'model': 'embed-english-1'}, headers=auth, timeout=30)

from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
with ThreadPoolExecutor(64) as ex:
    for i in range(800):
        ex.submit(make, i)
```

maya_sre: Thanks. I pulled runtime logs for the customer's shard around the spike window. Key snippets: 
```
[2026-02-14T03:12:08Z] batcher: slot_alloc id=42 size=64 queued=18 coalesce_ms=6
[2026-02-14T03:12:08Z] dynbatch: created_batch sz=42 max_batch_size=128
[2026-02-14T03:12:09Z] runtime: model_variant_switch to embed-english-1-quant (kv_cache flush)
[2026-02-14T03:12:09Z] runtime: long_kernels fallback, latency=9.4s
[2026-02-14T03:12:09Z] api: 503 to client after waiting on batch completion
```

maya_sre: Notably we see a variant switch and KV cache eviction in the middle of high load — that can cause very long token latencies as kernels rewarm. Also batch sizes are frequently underfilled because of the interleaved huge requests which increase per-item processing time.

nora_eng: Two things to check: 1) are we honoring the route-level `max_batch_size` override for this customer? 2) is dynamic batching slot preemption happening (small requests preempting slots because long jobs occupy GPU)?

ashley_support: Customer config: had default dynamic batching on, no per-route override. They expected runtime to coalesce small requests but not delay small-to-large mix.

liam_runtime: Quick mitigation options we can suggest to customer: 
- set `max_batch_size=32` for their embeddings route while they roll the client change (prevents huge-formed batches)
- set `coalesce_window_ms=4` (lower) to favor latency over throughput
- temporarily disable dynamic batching on that route (force immediate dispatch)

liam_runtime: From an infra perspective I'll also check whether the routing decided to fallback to a quantized variant due to capacity and that triggered kernel warming. If so, we need to ensure variant warmups or avoid mid-batch variant switches.

maya_sre: I see metric blips in `batch_fill_ratio` and `kv_cache_evictions` aligned with p99 spikes. Also `dynbatch_flush_count` went up during the incident window.

ashley_support: Customer is asking about billing — they saw retries increase token charges. Can we confirm how retries are billed and if we can retroactively credit the spike?

nora_eng: Billing side: retries produce additional billed tokens unless we consider them failed on our side (5xx). We should review if the 503s are internal timeouts; if they're on our side we can propose a one-time credit. I'll loop in finance after we confirm logs.

ashley_support: Customer approved trying the `max_batch_size=32` and lowering `coalesce_window_ms`. They asked for an engineered-root-cause timeline and whether there are safeguards to prevent variant switches mid-batch.

liam_runtime: Action items: 
- (liam) check variant routing decisions around 03:12Z and why a quantized variant was selected.
- (maya) gather exact `kv_cache_evictions` and `batch_fill_ratio` graphs for the shard and annotate times.
- (nora) confirm billing policy and advise on potential credit.
- (ashley) send the client the quick mitigations and ask them to run repro with `max_workers=16` to see impact.

nora_eng: Also propose a short-term platform change: add an atomic guard that prevents variant migrations for in-flight batches (ensures variant binding per-slot). If we believe migrations caused the warmup cost, this will prevent regressions.

liam_runtime: I dug logs: the quantized variant was chosen because primary nodes hit capacity and routing fell back to a lower-cost variant with different kernel path. It did happen mid-load but I don't see explicit per-batch migration events; likely slot-level binding didn't happen fast enough.

maya_sre: Repro suggestion for eng: run the attached python script with `--interleave=large:short=1:9` and concurrency 64 against a staging shard with a forced variant switch flag. We can reproduce the 7-12s p99s easily.

ashley_support: Customer applied `max_batch_size=32` and reduced concurrency to 16 as we recommended. They reported immediate p99 improvement (from 8s -> 1.8s) and no 503s in the last 30m. :tada:

nora_eng: Great. Keep eng-ticket open for the guard change and add an integration test that simulates interleaved long/short requests under variant churn.

liam_runtime: I'll follow up with a runtime PR to ensure slot->variant binding is enforced once a slot is allocated. Also will add a metric `slot_variant_bind_failures`.

sre-bot: Incident note created: INC-2026-0214-embed-batch-taillat. Assigned: liam_runtime, maya_sre, nora_eng.

ashley_support: Thanks team — I'm sending the customer the timeline and our next steps. I'll update this thread after finance confirms any credits.

liam_runtime: Closing loop: I saw one edge case where `max_batch_size` override didn't cascade to a specific autoscaled pool when config change was recent. Added a hotfix to the config syncer to propagate route overrides immediately. Will monitor.

maya_sre: Monitoring shows stabilized p99 across affected shard after hotfix. Marking as resolved on our side but keeping the eng ticket until variant-binding guard lands.

ashley_support: Customer confirmed billing was adjusted for spike. Closing customer-facing ticket. :white_check_mark:
